answer: In a market for pulse monitoring and velvet quality checks, use a fixed reward budget per customer task. Before workers submit, the customer commits a test whose hidden cases are revealed by a later random signal. Pay for distinct verified improvements, not the number of submitting accounts; identical or redundant outputs share one capped payout. A Sybil farm must produce additional useful results instead of collecting a joining bonus for each alias. Colluding customers can invent tasks, so independent spot audits remain necessary, and novelty tests can unfairly penalize honest similar work.
